I see they used a 26 MHz reference crystal. Very much a CB-first concept. It's built like a combination of a 1920s AM receiver and a 1960s CB radio wired into a chip made to send text messages over FRS.

https://x.com/i/status/2106475478940803490

2107920317813313775.a:
That is. FHSS and CDCSS have nothing at all to do with each other. Except both could be represented as a bit pattern. "Learn FHSS" presumably would tell the radio to learn the frequency hop pattern of a radio which supports that. It suggests maybe they have another radio which uses FHSS. CDCSS tells the radio the bit sequence code to unmute the receiver. A subsonic FM modem repeats the pattern over and over until the transmitter is ready to shutdown. A slight delay after the CDCSS modem stops is inserted to give the far side radio time to mute before the FM transmitter is brought down.
